description: Independently source-labelled targeted checks on immutable upstream snapshots. Selected labels form an open set, not whole-repository truth or a broad accuracy score. No target code is executed.

expectations.reason: Public prerequisite_tasks calls lookup_prerequisite inside its map on the same Task receiver; the method is explicitly private.
Public add_description and comment= call add_comment on the same Task receiver; the method is explicitly private.
Public full_comment and comment call transform_comments on the same Task receiver; the method is explicitly private.
The block passed by public comment calls first_sentence while transforming Task comments; the method is explicitly private.
Public/protected invocation flow references format_trace_flags in trace interpolation; the method is explicitly private.

limitations: Only five known-used helper facts are labelled; unreviewed findings are not automatically false positives.
Ruby command-security, whole-library deadness and independent recall are not measured here.

expectations.reason: Inline ingress at lines 91-95 declares TCP port 22 from literal 0.0.0.0/0. No count/for_each, overridden provider, or module expansion is needed for this declaration fact. README also independently lists CKV_AWS_24 for this resource.
Direct new DB has storage_encrypted=false at line 19; no snapshot/replica/restore/S3-import creation context, count/for_each or custom provider. README independently lists CKV_AWS_16.
This group has no inline ingress; its separately declared rules are evaluated as their own resources. This does not establish group or deployment safety.
Explicit type=egress; D400 is administrative ingress only. This does not earn safe/TN credit.
The bounded source model does not interpret numeric-string port fields; CIDR is also a resource-derived expression. Record unresolved policy coverage, not a safe/TN result.

limitations: TerraGoat explicitly is vulnerable-by-design training material, not production or deployment-accuracy evidence.
Declaration facts do not prove Internet reachability, Terraform application or account state.
Unknown and not-applicable expectations must not count as safe/TN outcomes; unsupported AWS resource families remain visible.
